options.title: Adjust rooming pace
options.description: Match rooming pace to physician capacity to reduce wait times. Ensure rooming continues only when physician pace allows.
options.local_fit: This option directly addresses the observed long room-to-physician time, a key contributing factor to the issue.
options.possible_pressure_transfer: If rooming pace is adjusted, pressure might shift to the Charge Nurse, who would need to manage rooming flow to align with physician capacity. This could lead to further escalation if rooming and physician pace are not properly synchronized.
options.how_we_would_know: Monitor room-to-physician time and bed occupancy. If this adjustment improves wait times, it suggests a successful fit.
options.revisit_or_stop_if: If room-to-physician time remains long despite adjustments, or if bed occupancy consistently remains above 90%, this option may need reevaluation.

options.title: Protect monitored beds
options.description: Ensure reserve monitored beds are available for acute arrivals by adjusting bed allocation strategies. This could involve prioritizing CTAS 1 and CTAS 2 patients.
options.local_fit: This option addresses the lack of monitored beds for CTAS 2 patients, a specific issue observed in the records.
options.possible_pressure_transfer: Pressure might shift to the Physician Lead, who would need to ensure sufficient monitored beds are available for acute arrivals. This could lead to further challenges if bed allocation strategies are not effectively adjusted.
options.how_we_would_know: Track the availability of monitored beds for CTAS 1 and CTAS 2 patients. If this adjustment reduces wait times for these patients, it suggests a successful fit.
options.revisit_or_stop_if: If monitored beds remain unavailable for acute arrivals, or if high bed occupancy persists, this option may need reevaluation.

options.title: Learn more about wait times
options.description: Bring the issue of long room-to-physician time to an existing huddle. Explore the root causes and potential solutions with a broader team.
options.possible_pressure_transfer: Pressure might shift to the huddle participants, who would need to engage in a collaborative problem-solving process. This could lead to a more holistic understanding of the issue.
options.how_we_would_know: Through huddle discussions and potential action items, we would gain insights into the root causes and potential solutions for long room-to-physician time.
options.revisit_or_stop_if: If the huddle identifies specific actions or strategies to address the issue, we should implement and monitor those. If not, further investigation may be needed.

recommendation.rationale: While all options have low evidence strength, adjusting rooming pace directly addresses the observed long room-to-physician time, a key contributing factor to the issue. This option has the potential to significantly impact wait times and is therefore recommended as the leading option.
recommendation.would_change_if: If the issue of long room-to-physician time is found to be primarily due to a shortage of physicians or a surge in patient arrivals, the leading option would likely shift to protecting monitored beds or learning more about wait times.

suggested_reviewers.why: The Charge Nurse is responsible for managing rooming flow and has direct insight into the room-to-physician time issue. Their input is crucial for understanding the local context and potential solutions.

The Physician Lead oversees physician capacity and resource allocation. Their involvement is essential for understanding the broader capacity issues and potential adjustments to bed allocation strategies.
